rule: A repair campaign may open an Issue and author a Plan against a protected surface, but it must never route that surface into automated planning, acquisition, execution, publication or closure. Protection is checked before dispatch, and a hit is a hard stop, never a warning.

capabilities.reason: Owns the campaign policy, host-grant binding and append-only journal. A campaign may report a defect in this surface but cannot route itself into automated repair.
Owns AcceptanceMatrixV1 and the product-acceptance projection that binds the existing AcceptanceReceipt. A campaign that could edit its own verdict authority could accept itself.

capabilities.surface: campaign policy, merge gate and worktree helpers
capabilities.reason: Owns .ai/harness/policy.json (where development_campaign.mode will live), scripts/merge-gate.ts, scripts/contract-worktree.sh and scripts/ship-worktrees.sh. A campaign that could relax its own policy ladder or the merge gate would defeat the activation ladder from inside a candidate branch.
Owns the untrusted-external-content boundary the campaign reads through. A campaign that could rewrite intake could launder its own Issue bodies into trusted facts.
Owns the delegation admission fence that keeps an injected coordination context from reaching a worker. The campaign consumes this fence; it must not be able to move it.
Owns EngineerOffer projection and the acquire revalidation the campaign's bounded parallelism depends on. A second scoring authority inside the campaign is exactly the drift this list forbids.
Owns the authenticated Engineer principal mapping and immutable ClaimActor receipts. This is the repository's security and credential surface; automated repair here is never in scope.
Owns the typed hook runtime that every host event passes through. A campaign-authored change here would change the enforcement path that is supposed to bound the campaign.

unmapped_surfaces.reason: Task identity derivation, the canonical backlog row grammar and the lease owner store are protected, but no archcontext capability include glob currently owns them; capability.runtime-harness.integration-acceptance only references coordination-lease-store.ts as a sink. Recorded here so protection does not depend on a capability node that does not exist.

PublicationReceiptV1 and MergeReadinessV1 are protected. The sprint architecture notes name capability.runtime-harness.publication, which does not exist as a node; these paths are reachable only as integration-acceptance sinks.
The protected helper that mints AcceptanceReceipt bytes. src/cli/runtime/helper-runner.ts already lists it in PROTECTED_HELPERS, but no capability include glob owns the file.

installed_capability.reason: BRC3 installed the campaign boundary while runtime policy remains off by default; the campaign is protected against itself.
